claims.explanation: Halcinonide is a glucocorticoid receptor (GR) agonist, and its selective killing is most likely driven by GR expression and downstream signaling. The L1000 virtual cell shows induction of the GR target TSC22D3 in responsive lines, and the most similar reference drugs are all GR agonists, confirming on-target activity. PI3K/AKT pathway mutations (e.g., PTEN loss) and chromatin remodeling mutations may further modulate sensitivity.

features.basis: direct target of halcinonide; GR agonist signature (TSC22D3 up) and similar drugs are GR agonists
PTEN mutations enriched in resistant lines; PI3K/AKT activation antagonizes GR-mediated apoptosis
PIK3CA mutations enriched in resistant lines; PI3K/AKT activation antagonizes GR signaling
ARID1A mutations enriched in sensitive lines; SWI/SNF modulates GR chromatin binding
BRAF mutations enriched in sensitive melanoma lines; MAPK crosstalk with GR
NRAS mutations observed in sensitive lines; MAPK pathway activation
SF3B1 mutations observed in sensitive lines; altered splicing may affect GR isoforms
SMARCA4 mutations observed in resistant lines; SWI/SNF loss may protect from GR apoptosis
RB1 mutations observed in resistant lines; RB1 loss may bypass GR-induced cell cycle arrest
